tasks.spec: You are working in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp; run `.venv/bin/python` (never uv). Run tests with `env -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov <files>`. No network, no live model call, no billed call. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. NO regular expressions in new code. No story vocabulary (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle, passenger seat) in non-test code. Write the tests FIRST, run them, confirm they fail for the right reason, then implement until they pass. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/web_demo.py, scripts/ringer/transcript_1a/live_baseline.py, the NEW files tests/test_web_demo_observation_enforce.py and tests/test_live_baseline_enforce.py, and tests/test_live_baseline.py ONLY to extend it for the new flag (do not weaken any assertion). Run ruff check and ruff format on your files at the end. BACKGROUND. `WorldCapture` (storygame/runtime/capture.py) has an optional `enforcing_verifier: ObservationVerifier | None` (default None). When set, the engine previews each narration candidate, asks the verifier whether the required things are really described, and on rejection uses the one shared recovery path with exact rollback; on exhaustion the turn is an unsuccessful turn. The mechanism is built and tested (tests/test_observation_enforcement.py, test_observation_preview.py) but nothing in the product sets it, so it is OFF everywhere. A live shadow sample showed the verifier passes its gate, so the next step is to be able to turn it on for a measured run WITHOUT changing any default. BUILD 1 (product switch, storygame/web_demo.py). In `engine_for`, inside the existing branch that builds `capture` (the `FREYTAG_WORLD_CAPTURE == '1'` and not scripted branch), after `capture` is created: when the environment variable `FREYTAG_OBSERVATION_ENFORCE` equals exactly '1', set `capture.enforcing_verifier = ObservationVerifier(capture_ask)` (import from storygame.runtime.observation_verifier; reuse the same `capture_ask` Jev client the capture already uses, so the guard/budget path is unchanged; construct a NEW verifier object per engine, never share one across sessions because it holds a per-turn request counter). Any other value or an unset variable leaves it None: default behavior must be byte-identical. The variable has no effect when capture is off or the provider is scripted. Do not read it anywhere else. Put the variable name in one module-level constant in web_demo.py. BUILD 2 (bench flag, scripts/ringer/transcript_1a/live_baseline.py). Add `--enforce` (default off). It is mutually exclusive with `--shadow`: both set is a parser error with a clear message. With it on, `_replicate` sets `capture.enforcing_verifier = ObservationVerifier(capture_ask)` right where `--shadow` sets `shadow_verifier`. With it on, each turn row gains `observation_enforce`: the enforcement-related part of `capture.last_after` for that turn (read what `after_commit` and `preview_commit` actually record, for example the `observation_preview` and `observation_diverged` keys; copy exactly those keys that exist, without inventing any) or None when the turn left `capture.last_after` unchanged (the same stale-record rule `--shadow` already uses for engine-authored move turns: reuse that mechanism, do not duplicate it). Also record per turn the count of narration attempts and the count of verifier requests if the engine/capture expose them; if they are not exposed without touching product code, record only what is exposed and say so in your final message. The summary gains `enforce: true/false`. With `--enforce` off, rows and summary must be byte-identical to today (add a test that compares). Do not change the route tables, the call cap logic or the `--shadow` output. BUILD 3. If a document in docs/ already lists FREYTAG_WORLD_CAPTURE or FREYTAG_FIXED_REFUSAL as a deployment setting, add one short row for the new variable stating: default off, hosted values need the owner's decision, enabling adds at most one Jev request per narration attempt. If no document lists them, add nothing and say so. TESTS (tests/test_web_demo_observation_enforce.py; follow how tests/test_web_demo_fixed_refusal.py builds the app and its engine with capture on and a stub Jev/provider; use monkeypatch.setenv; no network). Cover: a) unset variable: engine capture has `enforcing_verifier` None; b) value '1': it is an ObservationVerifier wired to the same ask the capture uses; c) values '0', 'true', '', ' 1': stay None; d) two engines built for two sessions have two different verifier objects; e) capture off (FREYTAG_WORLD_CAPTURE unset) with the variable '1': no capture, no error; f) scripted provider with the variable '1': no capture, no error; g) with the variable '1', an engine turn on a synthetic story runs through preview and a rejecting stub verifier gives an unsuccessful turn with rollback while an accepting one commits (reuse helpers from tests/test_observation_enforcement.py). TESTS (tests/test_live_baseline_enforce.py plus an extension of tests/test_live_baseline.py; follow the existing fake-Worker pattern in test_live_baseline.py): a) `--enforce` and `--shadow` together exit with a parser error; b) with `--enforce`, `capture.enforcing_verifier` is set and rows carry `observation_enforce`, summary `enforce` true; c) without it rows and summary equal the old output and `enforce` is false; d) an engine-authored move turn gets `observation_enforce` None. Keep each test short and independent.
